docs.a38e5531ae92: On macOS the stage plays along with the song, as it does on Windows: a Mac draws 3D on a real graphics card. Linux draws Oscillate's window with WebKit, which may be drawing 3D on the processor without saying so, so there the stage stands still to keep the app smooth, and says why: it draws a frame for each change — when you stop, move the playhead or change the view — rather than playing along, and the camera cuts instead of gliding. A Mac with no graphics card at all, such as a virtual machine, stands still the same way.
docs.a5c2d92c7274: The Spelling switch in the lane corrects a misspelled word as it ends. It is on by default when Oscillate is in English and off in the other languages, because the dictionary is English's, and your choice is remembered on this computer. Backspace right after a correction puts your word back. Completion and the tools below work the same with the switch on or off.
docs.a713154a6b75: Select a pad to shape its sound: its tune, a pitch sweep, an envelope, its pan, a filter and a choke group, and up to four Layers, each of which you can Reverse or Normalise. The layers take turns By velocity or In turn, a round robin. Reset to the kit's sound puts the pad back.
docs.a8522c985343: Press <kbd>Space</kbd> to start and stop. Drag a sound from the File Explorer onto a track, or double-click an empty part of a MIDI track to make a clip and start writing.
docs.a86f689c0403: Guitar Amp is an amp and a 4×12 cabinet with two voicings, Crunch and High Gain, and Input and Output trims of up to 24 dB either way. It goes on any track.
docs.aa8f79385db8: The Split Sheet is who wrote what, derived from the edit log, with work anybody undid netted out. It is a starting point for a conversation about credit, not a legal document, and it says so.
docs.ab1dee22b401: Ctrl+6, or View ▸ Stage, opens the stage: a 3D instrument and the hands that play a MIDI track on it, in time with the transport — through tempo changes, round the loop and wherever you scrub. It loads the first time you open it, so Oscillate starts no slower for having it.
docs.ab67452f2acf: Takeover — hand one track to somebody and take it back with one key. While they hold it they are the only writer for it, including you.
docs.ac2de81c2bb6: There are exactly three occasions on which it uses the network:
docs.ad0418c17aab: Layout chooses which drum each pad plays, the default or a mirrored Performance layout, and Fingers chooses the fingers the stage plays a pad part with, from one index finger to every finger.
docs.ae0ea2772a41: A sheet you open lies full width in the panel, its pages one under another. While the Sheets panel shows, 1 to 9 open the first nine sheets in the tray's order, 1 being the full score; the same key again, or Esc, goes back to the desk. A text field you are typing in keeps its digits. Every one of these keys can be changed in Settings ▸ Shortcuts.
docs.af2e3ba89e9f: The velocity lane under the grid has a handle per note. Ghost notes from any other clip can be drawn behind the one you are editing, which is how you write a bassline against a chord part without switching back and forth.
docs.b0013f90aea7: Chords turns each key into a chord in the project's scale: a triad, a seventh or a ninth, as Chord size says. It applies to every key that reaches the armed track — the hardware keyboard, the on-screen one, and the computer keys you type into it.
docs.b0bbcf140652: M and S: the track's own mute and solo, the same two as on its header and its mixer strip (Ctrl-click S to solo it beside the others);
docs.b13f8d00411c: A Drum Machine track stands as a 16-pad controller played by finger-drumming hands, its pads lighting as they are hit. Any other drum track stands as a studio kit played with sticks and feet.
docs.b2298073a265: Settings ▸ Plugins lists the folders being scanned and what was found. A plugin that failed to load is listed as blocked with the reason, and can be unblocked to try again. Oscillate hosts VST3 and CLAP; it does not host VST2 or AU.
docs.b24ba56ae294: Ctrl+5. Press Create a room code, wait for the code, and send it to whoever you are working with. They paste it, send you theirs back, you paste that into Let them in, and you are in the same session.
docs.b3307da67465: File ▸ Export companion folder… writes stems and MIDI that any other DAW can open. Stems line up at bar 1, so importing them somewhere else does not mean nudging thirty files into place.
docs.b36ebe696a5d: The Guitar Amp and the rock guitars
docs.b40583c5f830: Drag a .wav or a .mid straight from Windows Explorer or Finder onto a bar in the arrangement and it lands where you dropped it. MIDI goes onto MIDI tracks, audio onto audio tracks, and the wrong kind is refused with a reason rather than being given a lane of its own.
docs.b696ffb49270: Any MIDI track as sheet music, following the playhead.
docs.b94b8809bf80: Click a step to set or clear a hit. Drag along a row to fill the steps, or to clear them if the first one you pressed was set. Right-drag a box to take the hits inside it away, and drag back to put them back; a right-click on its own takes away the hit under it. Each drag is one press of undo.
docs.bb5fc5708305: Drag either end to trim; drag the top corner to fade.
docs.bea60461bd8b: Press Radar and Oscillate watches for pairs of tracks fighting for the same band — the bass and the kick, the vocal and the pad — and names the pair and the frequency. It costs CPU while it is on and the tooltip says so.
docs.bed27fa10d73: Open one of the first nine sheets, 1 being the full score, while the Sheets panel shows; the same key again goes back
docs.bfc4dfe30bdc: If the meter ever fell behind under load it says so — "the meter fell behind, so some audio was never measured". A number with no warning beside it means a complete measurement.
docs.bfcae0954b62: Ctrl+7, View ▸ Sheets, or the Sheets key in the titlebar shows the Sheets panel: any MIDI track as sheet music, following the playhead. It docks under the stage, over the editor, and is hidden until you open it. It always stays in the main window, because its pages turn on the main window's clock. Nothing of it loads until a sheet is first shown, so Oscillate starts no slower for having it.
docs.c06b71382c0f: Panels in windows of their own
docs.c281636fd984: Six devices are named and greyed with no controls, each for a written reason rather than a shrug. The analyser and the gain-reduction trace are not live.
docs.c379e75c7075: Drag the loop handle on the right edge to repeat it.
docs.c45ed4856c9f: The star on a row puts the instrument in Starred. In My Sounds, Save sound keeps the instrument on the selected MIDI track, with its settings as they are now, under a name and a folder of your own, ready to Add to any track.
docs.c474edeb7ac4: Four producers in a room, because every peer sends to every other peer and the fifth connection is where an ordinary home upload gives out.
docs.c4f07fe24936: Each row has M to mute it and S to solo it while the rest of the kit plays on, and a Choke group: a drum silences every other drum in its group, the way a closed hi-hat cuts an open one. On a Drum Machine track the rows are named by its pads, and a row's choke group is the pad's own.
docs.c61d0ae17869: A take you recorded travels. A sample you bought never does. When somebody joins a session that uses a sample pack they do not have, they get a list called Samples you need and the reason: Oscillate never sends samples between computers. Byte-identical is what piracy produces, and this product will not be a route to it.
docs.c6b2b316b1be: Every instrument row has a PACK key, which adds a one-shot of it to the One-shot pack under the browser, up to 25. Play each one, swap it for another take of the same instrument, or take it out. Export writes every one-shot in the pack as a WAV file into a folder you choose, and never writes over a file that is already there.
docs.c6f6907e5d27: Every instrument in the library has four envelopes you can switch on: Volume, Filter, Pitch and Pan. Each starts from a shape — Init, Pluck, Pad, Swell, Gate or Bounce — or you draw your own on its curve: drag a point, or double-click to add a point or take one away, up to 16 of your own.
docs.c763ac7681d9: The band along the top of the panel. The full score's chip comes first, then a chip for each MIDI track that holds notes, in the arrangement's order; when they outrun the band it scrolls sideways. Each track's chip carries:
docs.c7e25b23a89c: The pitch wheel bends the notes you are holding, and a note struck while the wheel is off its rest starts bent. The mod wheel and channel pressure bring in vibrato on the library's instruments. Hosted VST3 and CLAP plugins receive all three, as they would in any other DAW.
docs.ca2a0f41ebc8: Both themes, eighteen languages, and the choice you make wins over the machine's on the next launch. Right-to-left is real, not a text alignment. Speed and Reduced motion sit beside them: Quick turns the title twice as fast, and Reduce stops every animation, whatever the system says.
docs.cebcc1706c05: A count-in is set in Settings ▸ Recording. It is off by default.
docs.d1edfe59d41d: With no MIDI track holding a note, the panel says so. A track with more notes than a sheet can set keeps its chip, and its sheet names how many it plays and how many a sheet holds: split it into shorter tracks to read it as a sheet.
docs.d92b90c2dcd3: Roughly one connection in ten will not form without a relay, and Oscillate does not ship one — a relay costs bandwidth forever, and that is a running bill a free application cannot carry.
docs.dbb2a72d9b7f: Rap it, in the flow grid, times a recorded take you select on the track against the placed syllables, and marks each one early or late. It reads a take, never a microphone, and it generates nothing.
docs.ddbef0217d41: Around ninety scales. Choosing one highlights its notes, and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> moves whatever is selected onto it. Folding hides every row that is not in the scale, which turns a chromatic grid into one you can read.
docs.dde8792e71cd: Read the reason it gives — there are nine of them and they are different problems. Your network gives every server a different address means you need a relay, which goes in Settings ▸ Collaboration. Check that the code you pasted is the whole code: they are long, and a chat client that wrapped one will have broken it.
docs.df726c0bd8c5: Type - between a word's syllables, and _ to hold a syllable over the next note. On a track that plays notes, Split puts each syllable on its note, and each line shows how it fits the notes under it: 4/4 when they match, +2 for two syllables too many, −1 for a note left over. A line longer than its notes cannot be split, and says why; a word a rest breaks in two is named.
docs.e1403ae0c46a: on Windows and macOS, a grip that drags the track's MIDI out of Oscillate, onto the desktop or into another program. Click grips to pick several tracks and drag them together. The full score's grip, Drag all, drags every sheet's track.
docs.e19cbd5438b8: An update check, only when you press the button or switch on checking at launch. Off by default. See Updates.
docs.e2168f0fe102: Chat. It lasts as long as the room and nothing is written to disk.
docs.e2e4a9222290: Each MIDI track that holds notes is engraved on a treble, bass or grand staff, chosen from the notes it plays. The time signature and the key change where the project's do, each section marker gets a rehearsal mark, silent bars become multi-bar rests, and the pages look like paper, with the project's name and Page n of N. The staves are spaced by what they hold, so drum beams, a guitar's low notes over its TAB and the words never collide. Two hundred bars engrave in about a quarter of a second.
docs.e6513c30872c: Right-click a MIDI clip and choose Render to audio; right-click an audio clip and choose Convert to MIDI. Either way the result lands beside the original rather than over it, and one press of undo puts things back.
docs.e7b1751c9fce: The same clip seen as one row per drum instead of one row per pitch, laid out as a step sequencer. With Used voices only on, only the drums the clip plays get a row. Everything in the piano roll's table above works here too — it is the same notes underneath — and As a piano roll takes you back to the roll.
docs.e84f7ce0faa7: When the stage follows the armed track you can play it: click the piano's keys, a guitar's strings or the pads, and what you play on a MIDI keyboard or type into the piano roll's keyboard shows on the instrument. While a MIDI keyboard's pitch wheel, mod wheel or pressure is off its rest, a small readout shows it. Following any other track, the header tells you to arm it.
docs.e91f3b2dc496: Show or hide the File Explorer
docs.ea07e2f557fe: Humanize — push them back off it, by a little
docs.eadb0d7c2b3a: Each strip has the track's padlock too; see Locking a track.
docs.eb0eedb56328: With checking at launch switched off, nothing is contacted and the panel shows no result at all — Last checked stays Never. It never draws "you are up to date" over a check that did not happen, because those are different facts and only one of them would be true.
docs.eb1ebac609ad: Sixteen pads, laid out like a pad controller with pad 1 at the bottom left, playing one of four built-in kits: Sub, Floor, Neon and Wire. Each hit is chosen from three layers by how hard you play and alternates between two takes, so a roll never repeats itself exactly. Projects that used the Pad Grid open on the Drum Machine with their levels and chokes kept.
docs.eb8223ab78ba: As the song plays, the pages turn by themselves, keeping the line being played in view with the next one under it. The notes lit are always the ones sounding: a muted track lights nothing, while a track is soloed only the soloed tracks light, and on the full score each note lights on its own track's staff. The section list moves the playhead to a section, and every sheet turns with it. Page n of N says where you are.
docs.ebd61574858f: The window is borderless and Oscillate draws its own minimise, maximise and close. It opens clean: the transport, the Pattern Rack docked above the arrangement, and the arrangement. Every panel is shown and hidden by its key in the titlebar, by its item in the View menu, or with a key:
docs.ef86faf16227: Step the stage's view, forwards or back, while the stage has the focus
docs.f1972360c8eb: Faders, meters, the Masking Radar and the loudness panel.
docs.f28c2866474a: The cover gives the key, the tempo and the time signature, each change with the bar it comes at, the number of bars, and the notes in all and track by track. The credits name the writers, whose notes are still in the song, and the producers, whose clips or devices are, from the project's own history: under the names set in Settings ▸ Collaboration ▸ Your name in a room, or a collaborator's from their handle. Someone who never gave a name is counted, never printed as an id. Vocalists, samples and a label are left out, because the history cannot know them.
docs.f545becb9d77: Rhymes colours each line's last word by its rhyme, puts the line's letter in its section's scheme before it and the section's whole scheme — AABB, ABAB… — on its first line, and flags a stock phrase as common.
docs.f6ceafb1fe98: A report is written to your machine automatically. Settings ▸ General names the most recent one and opens the folder. The report contains the version, the operating system, the audio device and the plugin list by name — never your project, never a path from your disk, never a room code. It leaves your computer only if you choose to send it.
docs.f82da0230788: Kata are automation shapes you draw once and stamp anywhere — a swell, a filter sweep, a sidechain-shaped duck — so a gesture you liked is reusable rather than redrawn.
docs.f935e3c9c7fe: The type is meant to be sung from across a room, not read leaning in. Every lyric edit is an operation, so <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> takes it back like everything else.
docs.faf2ae9b7dc0: While the stage shows, <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> and <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> step the view the same way from anywhere, wherever the focus is.
docs.fb63caf27515: After that you are in a session called New Project. Nothing is saved anywhere until you save it, except the crash journal — which records every change as you make it so that a crash costs you nothing rather than costing you the afternoon.
docs.fc50699f9956: Pianos, guitars, basses and drums are each played by hands of their own. The factory Grand, Acoustic, Upright and Honky-Tonk Pianos, the Guitar, Nylon, Electric and Muted Guitars, and the Pluck, Slap and Upright Basses each stand as themselves, and an Electric Guitar into the Guitar Amp stands as a rock guitar. Any other instrument plays on the grand piano.
docs.fceb67e7d5a2: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>4</kbd>. A strip per track with a fader, a pan, mute, solo, the device rack and a meter that is drawn from the audio the engine actually produced — never from a prediction.
docs.ffbfdce6aedb: Lock: the track's lock; see Locking a track;

features.02a7818a6ee0: This page describes Freally Oscillate as it will be at version 1.0 — the rung the ladder ends on — and nothing planned after it.
features.0baacdf5d6c4: Your plugins, each in a process of its own
features.0c8436827b99: effects only, on the top plan
features.1b20c8037295: Freally Oscillate as it will be at version 1.0, beside seven commercial products as they are sold on 1 October 2026 — taken from each one's own product pages, shop, manual and support articles. Prices are list prices in US dollars.
features.1bcf2a5c1071: Hold more than four producers in a room. The fifth connection is where an ordinary home upload gives out.
features.1c110149d613: Lyrics as a lane on the timeline, locked to the playhead, imported from .txt or .lrc and copied into the project, in type meant to be sung from across the room. A 327,000-word dictionary completes and corrects as you type, each syllable lands on its note, and stress marks, rhymes with their scheme and a flow grid help you write. New in v0.10.0.
features.1c72614b8ea2: No account and no telemetry. It uses the network on three occasions only: a room you opened or joined, the address lookup while that room is set up, and an update check that is off until you switch it on. Crash reports stay on your disk unless you choose to send one.
features.1d662dd62590: A split sheet derived from who edited what
features.22f1bb054323: What you make with it is yours. Oscillate's author claims no ownership of the projects, MIDI, audio or renders you create with it, and asks for no royalty and no credit.
features.23131443a715: themes, light and dark, on Freally green
features.2dc43d70f9ea: A take recorded in the room lands on everybody's timeline. A sample you bought is never sent: the room sends the reference, and a collaborator without the pack is told which samples they need.
features.3592cc9add20: A crashing plugin leaves the session running
features.37e6fd7fe6f5: Relay a connection that will not form. Roughly one in ten will not without a relay in the middle; Oscillate names the cause, and Settings takes your own relay.
features.389cb06662bc: Side by side with the leading DAWs
features.3ab5583a8c27: The companion folder writes stems and MIDI that any other DAW can open, lined up at bar 1, in the format, sample rate and bit depth you choose.
features.3b50036d04c0: No beta on this page, no preview build, no early access. Until 1.0.0 the honest answer to “where do I get it” is not yet.
features.3b56c85ac1f3: Audio recording and a hardware MIDI keyboard on Windows, macOS and Linux. Takes stack under each other, you choose the parts you want, and the takes you did not choose are never deleted. Audio is written to disk as it arrives, so a crash costs the last block rather than the take.
features.40cbef707220: Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
features.45a1b4ecfbf5: A room with no server behind it
features.4c5f872abb2f: Hand a track to a collaborator, then take it back
features.4d7f4826526b: A strip per track with a fader, pan, mute, solo, the device rack and a meter drawn from the audio the engine actually produced. The Masking Radar names two tracks fighting for the same band and the frequency; the loudness panel shows integrated and short-term LUFS, the range and true peak against what each streaming service targets.
features.510ceece9d3b: The Drum Machine and the drum grid
features.52242b315ce6: Compiled on 1 October 2026. A “No” for a feature means it is not in that product's own feature lists, release notes or manual on that date. Products change, and this table describes them as they were then. Product names are the trademarks of their owners.
features.578fae09a667: Sheet music, TAB and the PDF
features.5fab46c33502: VST3 and CLAP. A plugin that crashes greys out its device and leaves the session running. Delay compensation is graph-wide and proved by a null test, and a plugin this machine does not have becomes a named placeholder, so a project opened somewhere else stays in time.
features.600105cd00bc: Every hosted plugin runs in a process of its own, and the application itself cannot even load one. A plugin that falls over greys out its device, and the transport keeps playing.
features.662d60837a2d: No server, so nothing to switch off
features.68481398e863: Who wrote what, derived from the edit log, with work anybody undid netted out. A starting point for a conversation about credit, not a legal document — and it says so.
features.6977b748edc2: Why it is built the way it is
features.6c8a2c880e29: Build a part row by row above the arrangement, clicking steps right in the rack: each row on one line with its track's own light, pan, volume and solo, and a graph of every step's velocity, pan, fine pitch and chance. Pattern mode loops the open pattern on its tracks' own sounds without touching the song, and Place pattern puts it in the song, linked. New in v0.9.0, polished in v0.10.0.
features.70a55e97f377: Your projects, audio and MIDI leave your computer only when you are in a room with somebody — and then they go straight to the people in it, not through anybody's cloud.
features.72db395b279f: All 1,648 instruments in folders by family, a star for the ones you come back to, sounds of your own, and an audition that plays the selected track's own notes through each instrument. PACK gathers up to 25 one-shots and exports them as WAV files. New in v0.9.0.
features.735112899b1c: Stated plainly, because a feature list that hides its gaps is not worth reading. Everything above is what version 1.0 is planned to have, and this is what still stands between here and there.
features.7d48e18b39c1: Host AU or VST2 plugins. It hosts VST3 and CLAP.
features.7e57d69f84a4: Draw a blade stroke across the arrangement and it splits every clip it crosses, the angle of the stroke setting the crossfade. Scrub the session's history like a video, and branch from any point in it.
features.7ffdfbe91dc1: A full DAW with a room in it: up to four producers in one session, live, with no account and no server.
features.85567c225aa3: A room code is the connection offer itself. With no server there is nothing to keep running, nothing to pay for and nothing anybody can turn off — which is also why a room holds four producers and not forty: every peer sends to every other peer.
features.8b5fc8a25fa8: Around ninety scales with highlighting, snapping and folding, ghost notes from any other clip, a velocity lane with a handle per note, lanes for how often each note plays and how far its velocity wanders, and a keyboard where one key can play a whole chord.
features.8d6419ade018: Six devices do what a plugin cannot, because a plugin cannot see the song it is in: a compressor already holding the chorus when it arrives, a gate that opens for a hit before it happens, a delay that empties into the bar line. None of the six adds latency.
features.908ec1ae94d2: The number you see is the number in the audio
features.956234fe74b6: Voice and camera with collaborators, built in
features.9f3893904d3d: Collaboration with no server and no account in the middle
features.a1eea7d00cdd: Use ASIO. On Windows the low-latency path is WASAPI exclusive, and Oscillate tells you which mode you actually got.
features.a6a1efe40897: Price on 1 October 2026, in US dollars
features.ae2bbaa95738: No AI, enforced by the build
features.af0df7623348: A crash is one device, not the session
features.arrangement.body: Unlimited audio and MIDI tracks, clips drawn from their own content, automation lanes, comping, groups, markers, and a tempo and time-signature map. Every edit is one press of undo however many clips it touched.
features.arrangement.title: The arrangement
features.b4a6bff8b8c9: Every figure is a count of what version 1.0 carries. Nothing is estimated and nothing is rounded up. Freally Secretarium plays the same instrument library as Freally MIDI Master: one library, pinned by both, rather than two copies that drift apart.
features.b6fc9acbd76d: Meters are drawn from what the engine produced, a knob's readout from the value the DSP is using, and a measurement that fell behind says so. Nothing on screen is a prediction.
features.b7d5af4a8c98: Several producers working in one session at once
features.b9277cfd1dc1: Unlimited audio and MIDI tracks, clips drawn from what they are, automation on every fader, pan and device control, comping, groups, markers, and tempo and time-signature maps. A pattern placed ten times is one pattern: edit it once and every placement changes, until you make one unique.
features.be31856f2db7: Hand one track to a collaborator and take it back with one key. While they hold it they are the only writer for it — including you — and that is enforced where edits are checked, not only in the interface.
features.c3ea64baf32c: Send a room code to whoever you are working with and up to three other producers can join your session: their cursors on your timeline, chat, voice, camera tiles and screen share. Peer to peer, with no account and no server in the middle.
features.c40c7b78e163: Hands on a 3D piano, guitar, bass, pad controller or drum kit play any MIDI track in time with the transport. Choose the camera, the quality and the skin tone, and play it yourself on the armed track. New in v0.9.0.
features.c7514e6ebfe8: track by track, through the cloud
features.ca873a2c8b0a: Any MIDI track engraved as sheet music in a panel of its own: treble, bass or grand staff, guitar and bass TAB with chord diagrams, drum sheets that say which hand or foot plays each hit, and the words under the notes. The pages turn with the song and light the notes sounding, and the whole song exports as an A4 PDF with a cover and the credits, or prints. New in v0.10.0.
features.cb2c6359ccf6: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> takes back your last change and never somebody else's, even while their edits are arriving. The edit log behind it is also the room's sync, Session Rewind and the Split Sheet.
features.cc88394d86d7: Knobs, faders and buttons rendered in Blender, light and dark on Freally green, short interface sounds you can switch off, and eighteen languages with real right-to-left — the same look in every Freally app.
features.cut.body: Draw a blade stroke across the arrangement and it splits every clip it crosses; the angle of the stroke sets the crossfade slope. It is the motion language the whole interface is built on.
features.cut.title: The Cut
features.d2a4cd186952: Every edit is an operation in one log. Undo, the room's sync, Session Rewind and the Split Sheet are four readings of it, which is why your undo can be yours alone and why credit can be derived rather than typed in.
features.d32646eadd7e: Share a screen from macOS. Screen share is Windows and Linux; on macOS the button is absent and says why.
features.d3a91a73c5cc: A beat battle mode in which each turn owns its own bars. The countdown is a countdown; the bars are the rule, so two computers can never disagree about whose edit was legal.
features.d48bbcde1043: apps for Windows and macOS; Linux in a browser
features.d6f79cef6f38: instruments and effects of its own
features.da9afac0d7b7: It is free today. All of it.
features.db3a0428cdec: No model, no inference, nothing generative. A build gate walks the dependency graph and fails on any inference runtime or model file, so it is a property of the build rather than a sentence on a website.
features.dbdcc26cbc1a: Freally Oscillate 1.0 and seven commercial DAWs, feature by feature
features.devices.body: Sixty-nine instruments and effects, with panels drawn from the device's own description — so the number on the knob is the number the audio is using, measured to a tenth of a decibel.
features.devices.title: Its own instruments
features.e2bfc1dfc118: Seventy-one devices, among them Freally Secretarium and its 1 648 instruments. Each panel is drawn from the device's own description, so the number on a knob is the number the audio is using, and a device's settings copy as one line you can paste into a chat.
features.e5498b8a441d: The short version: every other product on that table asks for an account, and each asks for money for its full feature set. Two of them let several people edit one project — Pro Tools track by track through its cloud, Soundtrap live in its own cloud. Oscillate puts four producers in one arrangement live, peer to peer, with no account, and it is free today.
features.e81deb2b9e8b: Sixteen pads on four built-in kits, each hit chosen by how hard you play, with up to four layers a pad, chokes, reverse and normalise. The drum grid is a step sequencer with swing and velocity, a Drum Map plays drums written for another kit on yours, and your own pad controller can learn the pads. New in v0.9.0.
features.ea63c07ebd35: A MIDI keyboard plays the armed track with transpose, a bend range, a velocity curve and chords in the project's scale. The pitch wheel, the mod wheel and pressure reach the library's instruments and your plugins. New in v0.9.0.
features.ef0a07e0d7a5: One shortcut renders a 1200×630 picture of the session to post. Session Timelapse rebuilds the whole session from its edit log as an animated picture with chapters — even a session nobody thought to record.
features.f997324cb19b: Every feature, for everyone. No paid tier, no trial that runs out, no licence key, no account and no in-app purchase.
features.fc8d60587699: Usable with no account at all
features.free.body: No tier, no trial, no account, no licence key. No model, no inference, no "smart" anything — and that is enforced by a build gate that fails on any ML runtime entering the dependency graph, not left as a promise.
features.free.title: Free, and no AI
features.kumite.body: A beat battle mode where each turn owns its own bars, and an authorship ledger derived from the edit log with work anybody undid netted out.
features.kumite.title: Kumite and the Split Sheet
features.pianoRoll.body: Around ninety scales with highlighting, snapping and folding, ghost notes from any other clip, a velocity lane with per-note handles, and a playable keyboard where one key plays a whole chord.
features.pianoRoll.title: The piano roll
features.plugins.body: VST3 and CLAP, each in a process of its own, so a plugin that crashes greys out a device instead of losing your session. Graph-wide delay compensation, proved by a null test rather than asserted.
features.plugins.title: Plugin hosting
features.room.body: Up to four producers, peer to peer, with no account and no server. Live cursors, chat, voice, camera tiles and screen share. Your undo takes back your change and never somebody else's.
features.room.title: The room
features.title: What is in it
footer.licence: Proprietary — All Rights Reserved. © Mike Weaver. Free to use today; future versions may be sold. Not open source.
footer.yours: What you make with it is yours. Oscillate's author claims no ownership of the projects, MIDI, audio or renders you create with it.
hero.headline: One session. Four producers. No server.
hero.tagline: A DAW where four producers work in the same session at once.
honest.ai.body: A build gate walks the dependency graph and fails on any inference runtime, any model file, and any analytics or crash-reporting library. It is a property of the build rather than a sentence on a website.
honest.ai.title: No AI, and how that is enforced
honest.code.body: It is the connection offer itself, and it carries your computer's public address. Treat it like a password: send it to the people you are working with and nobody else. The application says so at the moment you copy one.
honest.code.title: What a room code actually contains
honest.downloads.body: No beta on this page, no preview build, no early access. A DAW that half-works is worse than one that is not there yet.
honest.downloads.title: There are no downloads before 1.0.0
honest.failure.body: Some networks hand every outbound connection a different address, and two of those cannot find each other without a relay in the middle. A relay costs bandwidth forever, and that is a running bill a free application cannot carry — so Oscillate ships without one and lets you put your own in Settings. When a connection fails it names which of the nine causes it was.
honest.failure.title: Roughly one connection in ten will not form
honest.peers.body: A room holds four people. There is no server relaying audio, so every peer sends to every other peer, and the fifth connection is where an ordinary home upload gives out. Four is the number that works rather than the number that sounded good.
honest.peers.title: Four producers, and not five
honest.title: The things most sites put at the bottom
honest.updater.body: An update check, and only when you press the button or switch on checking at launch — it is off by default. It asks for one static file and sends nothing about you or your machine, every update is signed, and none is ever installed without your choice.
honest.updater.title: The one connection the application makes
ladder.intro: One line per rung. This is the same ladder the private plan follows — if one moves, both move, and a build gate compares them.
ladder.note: A rung that is done is built and on the development branch. It is not a download: there are none, and there will not be until 1.0.0.
ladder.rung.v0.0.1: Foundation, the CI spine, the licence and the EULA — and an empty window that already installs on three operating systems.
ladder.rung.v0.1.0: The shell and the audio engine. It looks like Oscillate and it makes a sound.
ladder.rung.v0.10.0: Sheets — engraved notation, guitar TAB, the sheet reader, lyrics under the staff, and the PDF.
ladder.rung.v0.11.0: Lessons — fifteen courses, Show me, and live listening through your own input, graded.
ladder.rung.v0.12.0: The studio's own — pitch moves, time stretch, live analysis, a doubler and a ducker, a master for each destination, and the final checks.
ladder.rung.v0.13.0: MixSir — the mix on your phone, paired from a QR code.
ladder.rung.v0.14.0: New devices, wave one — the low end and the groove.
ladder.rung.v0.15.0: New devices, wave two — instruments for the sound designer.
ladder.rung.v0.16.0: New devices, wave three — a record button that reaches back in time, and find-similar across your sounds.
ladder.rung.v0.2.0: The project and the arrangement view. It is a DAW.
ladder.rung.v0.2.5: The editors — piano roll, drum grid, automation, comping, the Cut, Kata, Session Rewind.
ladder.rung.v0.3.0: Plugin hosting and the stock devices — VST3 and CLAP out of process, and sixty-nine of its own.
ladder.rung.v0.4.0: The writing tools — the File Explorer, Stem-to-Generators and the export path.
ladder.rung.v0.4.5: The web go/no-go, the drop onto the timeline, per-device faces and exclusive audio.
ladder.rung.v0.5.0: The room, core — serverless connection, presence, sync and chat.
ladder.rung.v0.5.5: The room, live — voice, video, screen share, Takeover, Kumite and the Split Sheet.
ladder.rung.v0.6.0: Identity — the Lyric Lane, Session Timelapse, session cards and the credits page.
ladder.rung.v0.6.5: The family look, the same in every Freally app — Blender-rendered knobs, faders and buttons, light and dark on Freally green, interface sounds and a dark title bar — and one instrument library shared with Freally MIDI Master.
ladder.rung.v0.7.0: One engine — the shared audio and instrument crates pinned at one tag, the next rungs' foundations brought in, and the Freally family's cursor and toggles.
ladder.rung.v0.8.0: Freally MIDI Master, Flipcopy and Takelight in the box — stock plugins in the browser with a tutorial, MIDI Master's songs dragged onto the arrangement, and exports that carry hosted plugins.
ladder.rung.v0.9.0: The stage — 3D hands that play any MIDI track, a drum machine and a guitar amp, the instrument browser with all 1,648 instruments, a Pattern Rack that works the way FL Studio's does, and new knobs.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0: Stable and free, with Freally MIDI Master, Flipcopy and Takelight inside. Downloads open later.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0-beta: The beta — a new feature freeze, the whole app in one look and 18 languages, and this site rewritten. It repeats until the testing is done. No downloads on this page.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0-rc: The release candidate — hardening, the full review sweep, and every feature tested in the release app, in Windows' engine and in macOS's and Linux's. It repeats until one survives clean.
ladder.title: The road to 1.0
site.tagline: A DAW where four producers work in the same session at once.
what.p1: Every DAW is single-player software. Making a record with someone in another country still means exporting stems, uploading them, waiting, re-importing, and losing the thread — and six months later nobody remembers who wrote the bassline.
what.p2: Oscillate is a full DAW built around the opposite assumption. You paste a room code into a chat and up to three other producers drop into your session: you see their cameras, you hear them, their cursors move on your timeline, and when you are finished it prints a split sheet saying who wrote what.
what.p3: It is free today, and there is no server behind it. The room code is the connection offer, so the first person to join pastes a code and after that the room relays for everybody else. Nothing to keep running, nothing to pay for, nothing anybody can switch off.
what.title: What it is
